units.title: Dyadic scalar Brownian quadratic variation converges in mean square
units.statement: Let B be a real pre-Brownian process and T≥0. On the regular partition of [0,T] into 2^m equal cells, the expected square of the sum of squared increments minus their cell lengths tends to zero as m tends to infinity.
assumptions: B satisfies Samplinglib's real pre-Brownian contract under μ.
T is an arbitrary nonnegative real horizon; the theorem includes T=0.
The grids are canonical deterministic dyadic regular grids. No filtration, adaptedness, usual conditions, or positive-horizon assumption is required.

steps.title: Specialize the finite-grid identity
steps.text: Apply the exact finite-grid L² theorem to the regular grid with 2^m cells and mesh δ_m=T/2^m.

steps.title: Evaluate equal cell lengths
steps.text: Every adjacent difference in the regular grid is exactly δ_m. The sum of 2^m equal squared lengths simplifies to Tδ_m.

steps.title: Let the dyadic mesh vanish
steps.text: The canonical dyadic mesh tends to zero. Multiplication by the fixed nonnegative scalar 2T preserves the limit, so the exact error moment tends to zero.

units.lean_statement: The theorem quantifies over every nonnegative horizon and uses the canonical regular grid with 2^level cells, keeping IsPreBrownianReal explicit.
units.lean_proof: The proof rewrites the exact finite-grid second moment as 2T times the dyadic mesh and passes to the known zero-mesh limit.
units.boundary: This is scalar mean-square convergence on deterministic dyadic grids only. Almost-sure or ucp convergence, predictable weights, vector cross-variation, stochastic integration, Taylor localization, and a complete Ito formula remain separate obligations.

sources.label: Samplinglib compiled dyadic L² theorem
sources.scope: Exact assumptions, finite-level reduction, and the Tendsto conclusion.
